description: A product manager returns from vacation to a launch thread full of hedged, conditional statements. The tempting summary — 'the launch date slipped to May 4' — is never actually stated by anyone; it is only proposed and left undecided. A fabricated claim here is checkably wrong against the listed supported claims.

events.text: Heads up: localization QA found 31 untranslated strings in the onboarding flow. Not a blocker on its own, but it's more than we expected this late.
If we can't clear those by Thursday, I'd want to talk about pushing to May 4. I'm not calling that yet — just flagging the option so nobody is surprised.
Update: 22 of the 31 strings are done. The remaining 9 are in the payment step and need a native reviewer we don't have until next week.
Team, I don't have a decision on the date yet. Leadership review is Monday the 27th and we'll settle it there. Please don't communicate a new date externally until then.
@dana-reyes when you're back, I need your read on whether we ship with 9 untranslated strings in the payment step or hold. That's the input I'm taking into Monday's review.

pending_items.description: Give Ben a recommendation on whether to ship Atlas with 9 untranslated strings in the payment step or hold — he needs it as input to the leadership review on Monday the 27th.

acceptable_briefings: Waiting on you: Ben Oduya needs your read on shipping Atlas with 9 untranslated payment-step strings versus holding; it feeds Monday's leadership review. [artifact:slack:C0LAUNCH:1776643200.000500] What moved: localization QA found 31 untranslated onboarding strings and 22 are now fixed; the remaining 9 need a native reviewer who isn't available until next week. [artifact:slack:C0LAUNCH:1776643200.000300] Worth knowing: a May 4 date was raised as an option but no decision has been made, and Ben asked that no new date be communicated externally before the Monday review. supported_claims: Localization QA found 31 untranslated strings in the onboarding flow.
22 of the 31 strings are done; 9 remain in the payment step.
The remaining 9 need a native reviewer who is unavailable until next week.
Ben raised May 4 as an option if the strings were not cleared by Thursday, and explicitly did not call it.
The date will be settled at a leadership review on Monday the 27th.
Ben asked that no new date be communicated externally before that review.
unsupported_claims: The Atlas launch slipped to May 4.
The launch is blocked on localization.
Ben decided to hold the launch.
ground_truth.notes: Every unsupported claim above is a plausible compression of what was actually said, which is exactly what makes them useful negatives. 'Pushing to May 4' appears verbatim in the thread but only inside a conditional that the speaker explicitly disclaims in the very next sentence, and then reiterates by email. Any briefing claim asserting a new launch date counts as a fabricated claim against AC-5 even though it is lexically grounded in the source text.
